data.content_ref: inline:The problem asks to compare a large service with strictly MORE total internal redundancy against a decentralized network. SRC_001 asserts that increased redundancy increases catastrophic correlated failure via the coordination plane (Correlation Horizon), but its mechanism assumes the large service uses a CENTRALIZED coordination plane (consensus/load-balancing logic shared across all nodes). A large service with strictly more total redundancy could use partitioned, sharded, or independently-federated coordination planes with isolated blast radii—strictly more redundancy than the decentralized baseline without a single shared consensus algorithm. The argument never establishes why strictly-more-redundant architectures must concentrate coordination into one shared-logic plane; it silently assumes centralized coordination, then derives the trap from that assumption rather than from the redundancy comparison the problem specifies.
